newsitem.title: LEBANON: Mortar fired from south Lebanon slams into Israel.
newsitem.headline: Mortar fired from south Lebanon slams into Israel.

text.p: A mortar bomb or Katyusha rocket fired from south Lebanon slammed into northern Israel on Tuesday, a day after Israeli shelling killed two Lebanese civilians, Israeli security sources said.
No one was wounded in the attack. The army said it was checking the report. One military source said it appeared a round of 120-mm mortar fire had hit Israel.

Several mortars fired by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas from south Lebanon have hit the Jewish state this month, most apparently aimed at Israeli troops patrolling a 15-km (nine-mile) south Lebanon occupation zone.
Hizbollah guerrillas said earlier on Tuesday they had fired Katyusha rockets into Israeli and allied militia posts in south Lebanon.

In Lebanon, Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia sources said a number of Katyushas fell near the Israeli outpost of Blat and the SLA outposts of Dimeshkieeh and Risha inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, wounding two Lebanese civilians.
"The Katyusha rocketing was in response for the continued violation of April 1996 understanding which bans firing on civilians," a Hizbollah spokesman told Reuters in Beirut.

The April 1996 ceasefire understanding which ended 17 days of an Israeli onslaught on Lebanon in which about 200 people -- mainly civilians -- were killed, bars Israel and Hizbollah from hitting civilian targets.

Israeli shelling on Monday night killed two civilians in the village of Berti, east of the southern port city of Sidon. The shelling occurred after two SLA militiamen were wounded in a Hizbollah rocket attack on their outpost.
Israel carved out its south Lebanon occupation zone in 1985 to protect its northern border after withdrawing the bulk of its 1982 invasion force.
Hizbollah is fighting a guerrilla war to oust Israeli troops from south Lebanon.
